previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and obesity, was admitted for chest pressure and worsening shortness of breath. He had been recently discharged with a similar presentation and was found to have decompensated heart failure, with elevated BNP, pulmonary edema on imaging, and bilateral edema. He also exhibited episodes of symptomatic bradycardia and tachycardia on telemetry, leading to cardiology consultation and subsequent implantation of a biventricular pacemaker with ICD. He was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide, and had his beta-blocker changed to metoprolol tartrate for cost reasons. His diabetes was managed with insulin as metformin was held due to worsening renal function. He improved clinically, with resolution of symptoms and stabilization of vital signs, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged for device monitoring, lab work, and evaluation for obstructive sleep apnea.

Brief Hospital Course:
Discharge Weight 136.2kg

___ with Hx poorly-controlled T2DM (A1c 10%), HTN, HLD, CHF with 
EF 35%, cardiomyopathy, presents with chest pain and shortness 
of breath, found to have uncontrolled hypertension. 

# Chest pain and SOB:  Unlikely to be ACS, as EKG is unchanged 
and troponin elevation is consistent with recent ICD lead 
placement and levels were flat.  BNP is high but improved from 
prior, he appears euvolemic on exam, and CXR is improved from 
previous.  A trial of PPI for similar presentation during his 
recent admission failed to reduce pain or symptoms.  Concern 
that this is largely due to elevated blood pressure (150's/110's 
in ED which briefly required a nitro gtt to bring he diastolic 
pressure down).  He was started on lisinopril 20mg qd and his 
hydralazine dosage was changed to 50mg TID and his BP was well 
controlled at 119/81-137/96 with improvement in his symptoms.

# Hypertension:  The patient has significant difficulties 
affording medication, which has been a barrier to his medical 
optimization.  Given his CHF with EF 35-40%, CCB is not 
possible.  Only Toprol or carvedilol can be used of the beta 
blocker class.  He was previously on ACE (lisinopril 40mg), and 
Cr is elevated at 1.5, so this was resumed at 20mg qd.   
Hydralazine was switched to 50mg TID from qid dosing for 
improved compliance.  He will continue metoprolol 75mg BID, and 
his regular doses of torsemide, aldactone and Imdur.
 
# CORONARIES:  Recent cath in ___ showed a 60% LCx 
lesion. 
 
# PUMP:  Cardiomyopathy, sCHF with EF 35-40%.  Recent discharge 
weight 135.2kg.  On exam he appears euvolemic. He was continued 
on torsemide and aldactone with goal negative to reach discharge 
weight 136.2kg

# RHYTHM: The patient had a pacemaker placed ___ for 
tachy-brady syndrome.  Interrogation revealed normal function 
with no events.  He was monitored on tele without significant 
events and continued on metoprolol for rate control and his rate 
was well controlled in 60's-80's on the day before discharge.

#  T2DM:  A1c 11.1 in ___.  Metformin was d/c on prior 
admission due to elevated Cr.  He was continued on Lantus and 
ISS while here. Will follow up with PCP for better glycemic 
control. 
 
# HLD:  continued statin

# CKD:  Cr 1.5 on presentation, at recent baseline, okay to 
start moderate dose of ACE (lisinopril 20mg) but will need to 
have Chem7 checked as an outpatient within a week at his PCP's 
office

Transitional Issues:
Will go home with ___ for medication teaching and cardiovascular 
assessment.  Will follow up with PCP within one week and at his 
appointment will have chem7 checked to monitor renal function 
and potassium while starting lisinopril.
